market_view: Market is in a stressed, headline-driven regime: the S&P 500 fell 4.4% on Nov 5 (worst day since April 2025) on AI data-center fears after Democratic midterm wins, and today's +2.3% bounce looks like a relief rally ahead of tomorrow's October CPI. The Fed hiked in September, held in October with two hawkish dissents, and futures price a high chance of another hike in December; Fed speakers today (Goolsbee, Barkin) say the risk is on the inflation side. Leadership has rotated to health care, staples, payments and value, away from semis and AI infrastructure. Credit is softening (HYG lagging IEF by 2.2%), so I favour quality, low-AI-exposure compounders with steady trends over high-beta tech bounces.

positions.thesis: Health care is the clearest sector leader (+9% 20d, +12.5% 60d, 18% above 200d) and has little exposure to AI capex or rate-sensitive growth multiples; a defensive tilt that is not just more S&P tech beta in a stressed tape.
positions.exit_plan: Sell if it loses its 50-day average while the broad market recovers (rotation back to growth), or on adverse US drug-pricing policy.
positions.plain_reason: Health care companies keep selling when the economy and tech stocks wobble.

positions.thesis: Dominant GLP-1 franchise with strong, steady uptrend (+18% 20d, 27% above 200d); demand-driven growth independent of AI spending and rates. Today's FDA eye-condition label change applies class-wide and looks minor. Earnings well away (~Feb 2027).
positions.exit_plan: Sell if the thesis breaks (major safety or pricing ruling against GLP-1s) or the price closes clearly below its 50-day average; otherwise hold for weeks.
positions.plain_reason: Its weight-loss drugs are in huge demand and sales keep growing.

positions.thesis: Payment networks earn a cut of nominal spending, so sticky inflation helps their revenue; strong trend (23% above 200d), low AI exposure and high quality. Earnings Jan 28, 2027.
positions.exit_plan: Sell on a regulatory hit (card-fee legislation) or a clear consumer-spending slowdown, or a break below the 200-day average.
positions.plain_reason: It earns a small fee on every card purchase, and higher prices lift that fee.

positions.thesis: Same inflation-linked payments thesis as Visa, with slightly stronger momentum (+10.6% 20d, 22% above 200d); quality compounder outside the AI trade.
positions.exit_plan: Sell on card-fee regulation, a consumer-spending downturn, or a break below the 200-day average.
positions.plain_reason: Like Visa, it profits from everyday spending even when prices rise.

positions.thesis: Steady pharma and medtech grower in an uptrend (13% above 200d), defensive with low beta to AI and tech; reported in October, next report ~Jan 26, 2027.
positions.exit_plan: Sell on an adverse litigation or drug-pricing ruling, or a break below the 200-day average.
positions.plain_reason: A steady medicine and medical-device maker that holds up in rough markets.

positions.thesis: Membership-fee model and trade-down beneficiary when inflation squeezes consumers; strong trend (+10% 20d, 10.6% above 50d) with low AI exposure. Fiscal Q1 report expected around Dec 10 (estimate).
positions.exit_plan: Sell if monthly sales slow sharply, or if it gets too expensive once markets calm down and leadership rotates back to growth.
positions.plain_reason: Shoppers flock to its bargains when prices rise, and members pay yearly fees.

plain_summary: Keep money in the S&P 500 and test a few steady health and payment companies on paper.
